init.label: Computed columns: define a column, don't type it
init.body: A table column can be **Data** (literal cells), a **Formula** (a row-wise expression stored on the column), or a **λ** wired in from outside. Inside any row formula a column name already reads *this row's* cell, so `price * qty` multiplies this row's two. `@name` is Excel's `[@Price]`: the same row read, and the only spelling that reaches a value that ISN'T a column. Open the Sales table (click its chip) to see the per-column source selects; the chip's **ƒ** marks a table with defined columns.

init.label: Margin rule — its param names the column
Two defined columns in one table
init.body: `revenue` is a **Formula** column — `price * qty`, stored on the column itself. `margin` is a **λ** column bound to the wired Margin rule: `LAMBDA(revenue, revenue * 0.25)`, whose parameter binds to the column of that name — a computed column referencing another computed column, evaluated in dependency order.

init.label: @ over a wired list
init.body: Mid-pipeline, the **Computed Column** node adds `scaled = revenue * @scale`. `revenue` is a column, so it needs no `@`; `scale` isn't — an `@name` matching no column becomes a side input on this node, and the wired list is read **row by row** (it must line up: 4 values for 4 rows; a mismatch is a per-row `#SHAPE!`). A scalar wired there would read the same every row.
